title: AFP opens 2026 DAGITPA exercise with external defense focus

blocks.text: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Friday opened the 10th iteration of its Dagat, Langit at Lupa (DAGITPA) exercise, with a focus on strengthening the country's external defense and territorial integrity.

AFP chief General Antonio Nafarrete said the exercise aims to test the military's ability to conduct joint operations under realistic conditions, bringing together the capabilities of its different services.

"This security environment we face today requires an armed forces that can respond to threats to our sovereignty and territorial integrity," Nafarrete said during the opening ceremony at Camp Aguinaldo.

"This requires more than the capabilities of our individual services. We must be able to bring these capabilities together, make timely decisions, and carry out operations as one joint force," he added.
For Nafarrete, DAGITPA should be treated as a “mission rehearsal” rather than just another military exercise.

The exercise, known as AJEX DAGITPA 10-2026, is designed to enhance the AFP's ability to address current and emerging security challenges, particularly those involving territorial defense, maritime security, and cyber defense.

This exercise integrates the Philippine Army, Philippine Navy, Philippine Air Force, and Special Operations Forces to improve their capabilities in carrying out joint operations across land, sea, and air domains.

AJEX DAGITPA 10-2026 is scheduled from November 17 to 27, with major activities taking place within the joint operational areas of the Northern Luzon Command, Western Command, and National Capital Region Command.
The exercise has four major lines of effort: Command and Control Exercise, Field Training Exercise (FTX), Sustainment Exercise, and Humanitarian Civic Assistance.
FTX will cover three operational areas including Northern Luzon, West, and the National Capital Region.
Among the activities are integrated air and missile defense, air-sea battle, joint maritime strikes, maritime key terrain security operations, and counter-landing live-fire exercises.

For the defense of the West, the AFP will conduct operations focused on protecting sea lines of communication, securing offshore energy infrastructure, and testing anti-access and area denial capabilities.
Key areas include the Balabac Strait, Mindoro Strait, Pag-asa Island, and the offshore Nido Platform.

The exercise will also integrate cyber defense and information warfare scenarios to test the military's ability to respond to cyber-enabled threats and evolving disinformation campaigns. —VAL, GMA News
